workflow.name: Pull sources
workflow.description: Scheduled job gathers official mayoral releases, local reporting, broad web/news results, and public metric feeds.

workflow.name: AI extraction
workflow.description: Sources are summarized into announcements, promises, claims, topics, and evidence-backed next actions.

workflow.name: Human review
workflow.description: Low-confidence AI interpretations are flagged before they affect status labels or scorecards.

workflow.name: Visualize
workflow.description: Dashboard converts structured records into topic charts, progress bars, timeline items, and metric deltas.

sources.title: 311 Cases
sources.summary: Official San Francisco 311 cases dataset with request categories, subtypes, timestamps, and status fields; the connector filters it to Encampments requests.

sources.title: Overdose-Related 911 Responses by Emergency Medical Services
sources.summary: Official SF EMSA weekly counts of opioid overdose-related 911 calls responded to by emergency medical services.

sources.title: San Francisco Department of Public Health Substance Use Services
sources.summary: Official SFDPH dataset covering naloxone distribution, substance use treatment admissions, withdrawal management discharges, and MOUD clients.

sources.title: Building Permits
sources.summary: Official Department of Building Inspection permits dataset, including permit filing, issuance, completion dates, proposed use, and proposed units.

sources.title: Healthy streets data and information
sources.summary: SF.gov data story states quarterly tent/structure/vehicle counts and HSOC encampment engagement data are tracked in public dashboards.

sources.title: Office Vacancy Rate
sources.summary: SF.gov City Performance Scorecard describes quarterly office vacancy rate as a key downtown recovery indicator and says the data is available through DataSF.

sources.title: Five-year update to San Francisco Climate Action Plan
sources.summary: Climate Action Plan update framed around emissions, household costs, and city resilience.

sources.title: Union Square programming through summer 2027
sources.summary: Downtown activation and programming effort tied to tourism, foot traffic, and economic recovery.

sources.title: News from the Office of the Mayor
sources.summary: Official mayoral news page configured as a primary source for Daniel Lurie announcements.

sources.title: Homelessness and behavioral health response announcement
sources.summary: Coverage of Lurie's plan to overhaul homelessness, behavioral health, and addiction response.

sources.title: Emergency powers for fentanyl crisis response
sources.summary: Board action gave the mayor additional flexibility to speed up fentanyl crisis response.

promises.text: Create an emergency shelter plan intended to end unsheltered homelessness in six months.
promises.statusNote: Needs metric validation against PIT count, shelter capacity, encampment resolution, and outreach placement data. Marked delayed until verified completion evidence exists.

promises.text: Use emergency authority to accelerate city response to open-air drug markets and fentanyl-related street conditions.
promises.statusNote: Implementation activity exists, but outcome metrics need recurring public-safety and health datasets before completion can be assessed.

promises.text: Keep Union Square activations running through summer 2027 to support downtown recovery.
promises.statusNote: Clear deadline and output; completion should be checked against programming calendar, foot traffic, sales tax, and vacancy data.

promises.text: Publish and begin implementing an updated city Climate Action Plan.
promises.statusNote: Plan publication appears satisfied; implementation requires emissions, permit, building, and transport indicators.

claims.claim: Downtown activations can support San Francisco's economic recovery by bringing more people to the core.
claims.evidencePlan: Compare Union Square foot traffic, hotel occupancy, retail vacancy, sales tax receipts, and event attendance before/after programming dates.

claims.claim: The updated Climate Action Plan can lower household costs while reducing emissions.
claims.evidencePlan: Track utility costs, retrofit adoption, emissions inventory, and household energy-burden datasets.

metrics.label: 311 encampment requests
metrics.source: DataSF 311 Cases filtered to service_name = Encampments

metrics.label: HSH shelter waitlist
metrics.source: Needs a verified recurring public HSH shelter/waitlist dataset with stable API fields

metrics.label: Overdose-related EMS 911 responses
metrics.source: DataSF Overdose-Related 911 Responses by Emergency Medical Services

metrics.label: Naloxone distributed by SFDPH-funded programs
metrics.source: DataSF San Francisco Department of Public Health Substance Use Services

metrics.label: Housing-related building permits issued
metrics.source: DataSF Building Permits, deduplicated by permit_number for issued residential proposed_use records

metrics.label: Net proposed units in issued housing permits
metrics.source: DataSF Building Permits proposed_units minus existing_units for issued residential permits, deduplicated by permit_number

metrics.label: Office vacancy rate
metrics.source: SF.gov Office Vacancy Rate identifies a public downtown recovery indicator, but its stable DataSF API endpoint still needs schema verification

approval.label: Public approval proxy
approval.methodology: MVP placeholder until poll imports are configured; intended to be replaced by polling averages and survey data.

topics.label: Homelessness
topics.insight: Most important early promise area; needs hard public datasets before status can move from delayed.

topics.label: Public Safety
topics.insight: Implementation signals exist, but impact should be separated from enforcement activity.

topics.label: Downtown Economy
topics.insight: Good candidate for before/after visualizations because events have dates and measurable foot-traffic proxies.

topics.label: Climate
topics.insight: Plan publication is trackable; long-term implementation will need emissions and permit datasets.
